title: Pronoun order and agreement in the passé composé
goal: By the end of this lesson you can combine two object pronouns in the right order (je te le donne, je le lui dis) and make the past participle agree with a direct object placed before avoir.

body: Sometimes you replace both the thing and the person: *Je donne* **le livre** *à* **Marc** → *Je* **le lui** *donne*. Both pronouns go before the verb, in a fixed order.
The order depends on the pronouns, not on English word order: first *me, te, se, nous, vous*, then *le, la, les*, then *lui, leur*. (*y* and *en*, coming in lessons 47 and 48, always go last.)

head: Combination
Example
Meaning
rows: I tell it to him / her.

learn.tip: Me/te/nous/vous come BEFORE le/la/les; lui/leur come AFTER them.

body: Pattern A: person pronoun (me, te, nous, vous) + thing (le, la, les): *Tu* **me la** *prêtes?* (Will you lend it to me?) *Je* **vous les** *envoie.*
Pattern B: thing (le, la, les) + person (lui, leur): *Je* **le lui** *dis.* (I tell it to him.) *On* **les leur** *donne.*
Negative and passé composé follow the usual rules: *Je ne* **le lui** *ai pas dit.* With an infinitive: *Je vais* **te le** *montrer.*

learn.h: Agreement with avoir: the object that comes first
body: Normally a participle with *avoir* never agrees: *J'ai acheté une robe.* But when the **direct object** is placed **before** the verb, the participle agrees with it like an adjective (+e for feminine, +s for plural).
This happens with *le, la, les, me, te, nous, vous* and with *que* (lesson 53): *La robe? Je* **l'***ai acheté***e**. *Les clés? Je* **les** *ai trouvé***es**. *Elle* **nous** *a invité***s**.

learn.h: No agreement with lui, leur, y, en
body: Only direct objects trigger agreement. *Lui* and *leur* are indirect, so nothing changes: *Je* **leur** *ai parlé* (not parlés). *Je* **lui** *ai écrit*.
In *Je la lui ai donnée*, the agreement is with *la* (the direct object), not with *lui*.
In a positive command, the thing comes first, then the person, all joined with hyphens: *Donne-***le-moi**! *Envoie-***la-lui**! *Montrez-***les-nous**!
In a negative command, use the normal order before the verb: *Ne* **me le** *donne pas!* *Ne* **le lui** *dis pas!*

examples.fr: Le sel? Tu me le passes, s'il te plaît?
examples.en: The salt? Can you pass it to me, please?

examples.fr: Ta voiture? Tu me la prêtes samedi?
examples.en: Your car? Will you lend it to me on Saturday?

examples.fr: La nouvelle? Je la lui ai dite ce matin.
examples.en: The news? I told it to him / her this morning.
examples.note: la + lui; dite agrees with la

examples.fr: Les photos? Je vous les envoie ce soir.
examples.en: The photos? I'll send them to you tonight.

examples.fr: Le livre? Je le leur ai rendu.
examples.en: The book? I gave it back to them.
I'm going to show it to you.

examples.fr: Il ne nous l'a pas expliqué.
examples.en: He didn't explain it to us.
examples.note: negative passé composé with two pronouns

examples.fr: Ta lettre? Je l'ai lue deux fois.
examples.en: Your letter? I read it twice.
examples.note: lue: feminine agreement with l' (la lettre)

examples.fr: Les filles? Je les ai vues au parc.
examples.en: The girls? I saw them at the park.

examples.note: ouverte: you can hear the agreement

examples.fr: Mes clés, je les ai mises sur la table.
examples.en: My keys, I put them on the table.
examples.note: mises: agreement is audible with -s/-t participles

examples.fr: Elle nous a invités à souper.
examples.note: nous = direct object, so invités agrees

examples.fr: Je leur ai téléphoné, mais je ne les ai pas vus.
examples.en: I phoned them, but I didn't see them.

examples.fr: Cette chanson, je l'ai apprise par cœur.
examples.en: That song, I learned it by heart.
examples.note: appris → apprise: the s is pronounced

quebec.intro: Spoken French, in Quebec and elsewhere, takes shortcuts that writing does not allow: the 'le' in 'le lui' disappears, the command order flips, and many participle agreements are simply not pronounced. Know the written rule, recognise the spoken shortcut.

items.note: le disappears and lui becomes y; informal
very common in speech everywhere; write donne-le-moi
les dropped (and with it the agreement) in speech; informal
the agreement is often skipped in speech; always write it

drills.q: Choose the correct order: 'Il ___ donne.' (it to me)
Choose the correct order: 'Je ___ envoie.' (them to her)

drills.why: Les = les fleurs (f pl) comes before avoir: achetées.

drills.q: Which sentence has a correct participle?
La maison? Ils l'ont ___ l'an passé. (vendre)
drills.en: The house? They sold it last year.

drills.q: Les gâteaux? Je ___ leur ai apportés. (them)
drills.en: The cakes? I brought them to them.
Your dress? Will you lend it to me?

drills.q: Elle nous a ___ chez elle. (inviter, we = two men)
drills.en: She invited us to her place.
drills.why: Nous is the direct object before avoir: invités.

drills.en: I'm going to show it to you.
He didn't tell it to them.
drills.a: Il ne le leur a pas dit.

drills.why: Le/la before lui; agreement with la.
Negative command: pronouns before the verb.

a: Les lettres? Je les ai écrites.
drills.why: Écrit → écrites: agreement with les (f pl).

pron.tip: juh-luh-lwi-DI, keep it smooth; casual speech drops the first e: j'le lui dis.
Masculine ends in [r], feminine adds a [t]: oo-VÈR / oo-VÈRT.
MI vs MIZ: the feminine adds a [z] sound.
don-luh-MWA; the spoken version donne-moi-le is don-mwa-LUH.

dialogue.fr: As-tu donné le cadeau à Julie?
dialogue.en: Did you give the gift to Julie?

dialogue.fr: Oui, je le lui ai donné hier soir.
dialogue.en: Yes, I gave it to her last night.

dialogue.fr: Pis la carte? Tu l'as écrite?
dialogue.en: And the card? Did you write it?

dialogue.fr: Oui, je l'ai écrite et je l'ai mise dans la boîte.
dialogue.en: Yes, I wrote it and I put it in the box.

dialogue.fr: Elle a aimé les boucles d'oreilles?
Elle les a adorées! Elle les a mises tout de suite.
dialogue.en: She loved them! She put them on right away.

dialogue.fr: Super. Tu peux me montrer la photo?
dialogue.en: Great. Can you show me the photo?
Hang on, I'll send it to you. There!

questions.q: When did B give the gift?
What does B do at the end?

speak.prompt: Answer with two pronouns: 'Tu prêtes ta voiture à ton frère? Tu me donnes ton numéro? Tu as dit la nouvelle à tes parents?'
speak.model: Oui, je la lui prête. Oui, je te le donne. Non, je ne la leur ai pas encore dite.

speak.prompt: Ask a friend for three things with positive commands: pass me the salt, show me the photo, give me the keys.
Say 'I told him' the written way (je le lui ai dit), then the way you'll hear it in Quebec.
speak.model: Je le lui ai dit. / J'y ai dit.

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about things you lent, gave or sent to people recently. Use at least two double pronouns and make every participle agree correctly.
write.model: La semaine passée, ma voisine m'a demandé mon échelle. Je la lui ai prêtée tout de suite. Mes vieux livres? Je les ai donnés à la bibliothèque. Ma sœur voulait mes photos de vacances, alors je les lui ai envoyées. Mon frère m'a emprunté vingt dollars, mais il ne me les a pas encore rendus!

quiz.why: L' = la fenêtre (f), placed before avoir.

quiz.q: When does a participle with avoir agree?
options: When a direct object comes before it
quiz.why: Agreement with a preceding direct object (le, la, les, me, te, que…).

quiz.q: Standard written form of 'Give it to me!'
quiz.why: Positive command: le before moi in writing.

quiz.q: In Quebec speech, 'J'y ai dit' replaces…
quiz.why: Le is dropped and lui becomes y.
Pris / prise: the feminine adds a [z] sound.
Te before le; le becomes l' before a vowel: te l'expliquer.
